title: Database Performance and Reliability
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of database performance and reliability in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Query efficiency and Indexing and query plans.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study database performance and reliability as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 77 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Database Performance and Reliability matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP applications commonly use ADO to access relational databases through a provider. For 'Database Performance and Reliability', validate inputs, prefer `ADODB.Command` parameters for values, close Recordsets and Connections, and handle failures without exposing the query, connection string, or database details. Parameter syntax, supported types, cursor behavior, and connection string details can vary by provider; verify them against the installed driver and database.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Query efficiency; Indexing and query plans; Avoiding unnecessary database round trips; Limiting result sets; Connection and command timeouts; Handling database outages; Avoiding excessively large Recordsets. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Database Performance and Reliability
content_blocks.code:
Performance baseline:
1. count database round trips
2. limit rows/columns
3. inspect indexes/query plan
4. set command/connect timeouts
5. measure p50/p95 latency with representative data
content_blocks.expected_output: Measure query behavior before and after a change instead of assuming that a rewrite is faster.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Avoid logging user data or credentials. A timeout is a failure boundary, not permission to retry an unsafe state-changing operation blindly. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use synthetic records in a local test database and a least-privilege database account. Record the database/provider version and verify both success and failure cases. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of database performance and reliability. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of database performance and reliability using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Query efficiency. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

task: Build a short demonstration of database performance and reliability using synthetic data. Demonstrate “Query efficiency”, state the expected result, and document one edge/failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: Expected result is written before verification.
At least one invalid or boundary case is documented.
Runtime/provider/version assumptions and security limits are recorded.
hints: Start with the smallest example for query efficiency.
Keep the sample synthetic and change one thing at a time.
Compare observed behavior against a written expectation and consult the linked official reference if the runtime differs.

A reproducible legacy-code example records input, environment/version, expected outcome, observed outcome, and a meaningful failure case.
expected_output: Measure query behavior before and after a change instead of assuming that a rewrite is faster.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
